subject: Day 46: book the 100-day photos
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 46. The 100-day photo window lands around days 95 to 105, when Avi is smiling and head-steady but not yet rolling out of poses. Top photographers book out weeks ahead, so reserving now is the cheap insurance.

Action items
- Book the 100-day photographer now for the week 14-15 window; he will be smiling and head-controlled by then, and the best studios fill six weeks out. Schedule it around his nap and feed times to maximize the alert stretch.
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is booked within the next one to two weeks and keep a running feeding and output log to bring.
- If returning to work, confirm the daycare or nanny start date with a three-to-five-day overlap with the primary caregiver for a clean transition.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Posed-shoot interruptions from feeds, blowouts, or fussiness are routine; pad the session schedule accordingly.
- [low concern] Varied cooing and gurgling expanding day to day as the vocal range widens.
- [monitor] No social smile yet; it is still within range now but note it so you can raise it at the 2-month visit if it has not appeared by week eight.
- [call within 24h] A cluster of poor feeding, unusual lethargy, and decreased wet diapers together.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C), refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, or breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest. Call 911 for blue lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Prop a high-contrast or simply illustrated board book open in front of him during tummy time so head-lifting earns a visual payoff and prone time lasts longer. AAP HealthyChildren on baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Keep coo conversations going: when he gurgles, answer as if he spoke, pause, then respond to his next sound; this serve-and-return turn-taking predicts later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Close the day with the same lights-out song you started this week to reinforce the sleep-onset cue.

Upcoming
- Day 49: 2-month visit prep; build the question list.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines.
- Day 57-72: post-vaccine 24-48 hour fussiness and low-grade fever window.
- Day 95-105: 100-day photo session window.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
